idiom_name: helpers registered with the view engine next to the view (functions, tag classes or context objects)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the template declarative and put each piece of processing logic into a helper the template can invoke - a function in a presentation module, a component registered under a template name, or an object placed in the render context. Helpers should be pure: they receive the data they format and return display-ready values or fragments, and they must not fetch data, reach session or request state, or write output. Retrieval stays behind the controller/service boundary (in the source, a business delegate or a value bean that the controller puts into the view's model) so the helper only adapts and formats. Register helpers once per application or engine so every view resolves the same set, and let the engine's escaping apply unless a helper deliberately returns markup through the engine's safe API.
pitfalls: Helpers that retrieve their own data make rendering slow and non-repeatable; keep retrieval in the controller or a delegate.
An engine that escapes output will also escape a helper's markup unless the helper explicitly marks it safe - marking everything safe recreates the injection risk.
Helper names become part of the template contract; renaming one without updating the registry fails at render time in dynamic engines.

Wrong move: including a view helper module into a controller, model or service so its logic can be reused there -> the helper drags view context and its whole public surface into the wrong layer (in Rails an included module's methods can even surface as controller actions) -> instead keep helpers view-only, reach them through a helpers proxy if a controller truly needs one, and move non-presentation logic into a plain class or concern that the helper calls.

Wrong move: building whole widgets - label, input, wrapper - by string concatenation inside one helper -> the markup becomes invisible to whoever owns templates, semantics and accessibility drift, and the helper turns into an untestable HTML blob builder -> instead keep helpers to small value transformations and put repeated or evolving fragments into partials, includes or components.

Wrong move: pulling request, session or template-context globals into a helper instead of taking arguments -> the helper cannot be unit-tested, previewed or reused on another channel and its dependencies are invisible at the call site -> instead pass every input as an explicit argument and touch engine context only where the engine requires it (e.g. inclusion tags).
